ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF THE SPECIAL CAPITAL REGION PROVINCE OF JAKARTA
NUMBER 8 OF 2011
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and honor.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as participation of the business world and community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

1.9.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation explicitly covers exploitation that includes prostitution and slavery-like practices. In the PENJELASAN (elucidation) for Pasal 3 huruf a / definisi perdagangan orang, it states exploitation includes “pelacuran” (prostitution), “kerja atau pelayanan paksa” (forced labor/services), and “perbudakan atau praktek serupa perbudakan” (slavery or practices similar to slavery), plus “pemanfaatan fisik seksual organ reproduksi” (sexual exploitation of reproductive organs). This is sufficient to say the policy’s scope includes sexual exploitation/sexual slavery-like conduct. Therefore a “Yes” is supported by the Indonesian source, making the golden ‘No’ likely incorrect.

5.2.evaluator_rationale: While the text mentions 'religious leaders' as possible providers of assistance and references 'spiritual guidance,' none of the provided passages explicitly describe stakeholder engagement or collaboration with religious organisations/leaders as partners in services or prevention.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his position also serves as the representative of the Government in the DKI Jakarta Province region.
5. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Work Unit of Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Work Unit of Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and for or neglect of the household including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, handling and empowerment.
17. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children from occurring.
18. 19. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of trafficking in persons in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family is a person who has blood relations in a straight line upward or downward and collateral lines up to the third degree, or who has marital relations, or a person who is a dependent of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

So the main failure is retrieval not providing the most directly relevant phrasing for religious engagement.

On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as participation of the business world and community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his position also serves as the representative of the Government in the DKI Jakarta Province region.
5. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Work Unit of Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Work Unit of Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, both individual and collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and for or neglect of the household including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, handling and empowerment.
17. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children from occurring.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of trafficking in persons in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family is a person who has blood relations in a straight line upward or downward and collateral lines up to the third degree, or who has marital relations, or a person who is a dependent of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
